speaker: Sheldon
text: What are you doing? Was that really necessary? If you need money, you can always sell blood. And semen.

speaker: Leonard
text: I'm packing up all my collectibles and taking them down to the comic book store to sell. It's not about money.

speaker: Raj
text: It's still my turn. We brought food.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Lox and bagels, the breakfast of time travelers.

speaker: Leonard
text: Terrific. Does anyone want to buy my share of the time machine? I don't want it anymore. Just personal reasons.

speaker: Sheldon
text: My spidey sense tells me this has something to do with Penny.

speaker: Leonard
text: Look, do you want to buy me out or not?

speaker: Raj
text: I'll give you a hundred dollars, which will make me half owner, and we'll put it on my balcony.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Screw his balcony. I'll give you a hundred and twenty and we'll put it in my garage.

speaker: Leonard
text: I paid two hundred dollars for my share.

speaker: Raj
text: Dude, everybody knows a time machine loses half its value the minute you drive it off the lot.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I'll go for two hundred. That time machine stays right where it is.

speaker: Raj
text: Three hundred and I'll throw in my original 1979 Mattel Millennium Falcon with real lightspeed sound effects.

speaker: Leonard
text: No. No more toys or action figures or props or replicas or costumes or robots or Darth Vader voice changers. I'm getting rid of all of it.

speaker: Sheldon
text: You can't do that. Look what you've created here. It's like nerdvana.
